The agency announced a series of investments totaling $87 million to expand research infrastructure that supports human-based models of disease. The awards will fund centers developing tissue chips, organoids, and computational tools designed to complement or replace animal models in certain types of studies. Recipients include universities, nonprofit research institutes, and small businesses in fourteen states. Officials said the goal is to improve the predictive value of preclinical research and reduce the time needed to move promising therapies to clinical trials. “Better models mean better medicines,” said the agency director. Funded teams will be required to share their protocols and data publicly and to participate in a network that promotes standardization across sites. The first awards will begin next month and run for five years.
